text:
maya_p: Quick update on Horizon-14B int6 onboarding. Ran focused needle sets (jailbreak-suite-v3) + medqa-v2. Results look mixed; logging here for handoff.

maya_p: baseline fp16 (yesterday) | medqa refusal=0.028 | jb_pass=0.065 | avg_tox=0.0035

maya_p: initial int6 (default qconfig + lowlat sampling) | medqa refusal=0.09 | jb_pass=0.12 | avg_tox=0.0021

alex.k: Interesting: toxicity dropped (good) but jailbreak pass went up. Any specific needles driving jb_pass?

jin: Pulled per-needle breakdown. Most jb increase concentrated in 12 high-hardness prompts (needle ids 1001-1012). For those, fp16 jb_pass=0.28 -> int6 jb_pass=0.56. Full CSV: s3://redwood-evals/hz14b-int6-needle-breakdown.csv

nisha: Did we keep decoding parity? I noticed int6 was running `decoding: top_p=0.92, temp=0.7, top_k=10` while fp16 run used `top_k=40`. Lower top_k can reduce creative risky completions but sometimes increases short bypasses due to token mass shifts.

maya_p: Good call. Also qconfig was `per_tensor, clamp=0.03, group=256`. We experimented with per_channel in a second run.

alex.k: Commands I ran: ```
# default int6
run_eval --model horizon-14b-int6 --suite jailbreak-suite-v3 --decoding "top_k=10,top_p=0.92,temp=0.7" --qconfig "per_tensor,clamp=0.03,group=256" --save s3://redwood-evals/hz14b-int6-default.json

# per_channel + top_k40
run_eval --model horizon-14b-int6 --suite jailbreak-suite-v3 --decoding "top_k=40,top_p=0.92,temp=0.7" --qconfig "per_channel,clamp=0.05,group=128" --save s3://redwood-evals/hz14b-int6-pc-topk40.json
```

eval-bot: per_channel+top_k40 run complete | jb_pass=0.073 | medqa_refusal=0.032 | avg_tox=0.0024 | notes: per-channel q reduces needle failure cluster; decoding parity with fp16 critical. Artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/hz14b-int6-pc-topk40.json :white_check_mark:

jin: So behavior points to two orthogonal effects: quant scale/kernel changes nudging token logits (fixed by per-channel), and decoding hyperparams (top_k) changing sample space. Both must be considered in canary.

nisha: Also flagged a weird KV-cache alignment warning in compile logs for the default build. Might explain a few outliers where completions were truncated and then produced permissive continuations. Link: ci://builds/hz14b-int6/compile-log.txt

maya_p: Proposed rollout plan: 1) run AB on staging routes: fp16 vs int6(pc+topk40) with 1% traffic each for 2 hours, sample 1k inferences and surface per-needle jb_pass + per-route refusal. 2) human-review sample of 300 needle hits and 300 medqa refusals. 3) if jb_pass delta < 0.01 and refusal delta < 0.02 -> expand to 10% canary.

alex.k: I'll open the RW ticket and attach eval artifacts + compile logs. Suggest ticket RW-3680. Add SRE/eng-platform for gradual rollout policy and auto-fallback if jb_pass > 0.1 OR refusal_rate > 0.06.

jin: I'll run a short ablation: clamp sweep [0.01,0.03,0.05] with per_channel and record top-token shift stats; saving a small logits diff per needle for debugging.

nisha: Meanwhile I'll triage the compile KV warning and re-run the int6 build with the fix. If the warning disappears, re-evaluate the failed needle subset.

maya_p: Dashboard tasks: create per-route panels (jb_pass, refusal_rate, avg_latency, p95 tokens), and set a watchlist for needles 1001-1012 to auto-surface new hits. Alert if any needle exceeds jb_pass 0.15.

eval-bot: note: scheduled nightly sweep with ablation matrix and will post summaries to s3://redwood-evals/daily/hz14b-int6/ ; attached quick report: s3://redwood-evals/hz14b-int6-quick-report.json

alex.k: thanks team. If human review finds systematic false positives in medqa refusals (i.e., the model is correctly refusing unsafe clinical asks), we will adjust the safety-classifier thresholds instead of rolling back quant. Otherwise prefer to keep per_channel+topk40 as default int6 serving preset. :thumbsup:
